   120	\section{The domain of the paired-line helper}
   121	
   122	The prerequisite paired-line lemma, \path{lem:qld-xz-lines}, concerns two
   123	lines $\ell_X,\ell_Z$ in $\F_q^m$.  It constructs the POVM
   124	$\{T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\}$ with degree-$md$ polynomial outcomes,
   125	of degree at most $d$ on an axis-parallel component, and asserts
   126	\[
   127	  \big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{[f_X(x)=a,\,f_Z(z)=b]}\big)_{\mathsf A\mathsf A'}
   128	  \simeq_{\delta_P}
   129	  \big(\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\big)_{\mathsf B\mathsf A''},
   130	  \qquad \delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q),
   131	\]
   132	on the expanded state, averaged over two independently sampled line-point
   133	pairs, together with all symmetric equivalents.  The point measurements here
   134	are those of \path{lem:qld-4-10}, with error
   135	$\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$.%
   136	\footnote{Both statements occur in
   137	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}:
   138	\path{lem:qld-xz-lines} at lines~882--894 and \path{lem:qld-4-10} at
   139	lines~689--709.  Their blueprint nodes have the same labels in
   140	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex}.}
   141	This prerequisite is distinct from the extended-line lemma
   142	\path{lem:qld-4-13}, which constructs $\hat Q^\ell$ for a single line in
   143	$\F_q^{2m+2}$.  The domain repair below concerns the paired-line helper;
   144	it neither changes nor resolves the extended-line error discrepancy.
   145	
   146	The paired-line source statement does not take an arbitrary joint point
   147	measurement as an input.  Consequently,
   148	an internal theorem which accepts an already constructed point witness must retain
   149	the same quantitative dependency: it should first fix a function
   150	$\delta_Q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying the one-variable polynomial-error
   151	predicate, then choose $\delta_P$, and at strategy error $\eps$ accept only a
   152	point witness with bound $\delta_Q(\eps)$.
   153	
   154	Before the repair tracked by \ghissue{389}, the Lean helper
   155	\path{exists_combinedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness} instead had the quantifier
   156	order
   157	\[
   158	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   159	  \forall\eps\ \forall\delta_Q\ \forall Q,
   160	  \qquad Q\text{ has point error at most }\delta_Q
   161	  \Longrightarrow T\text{ has line error at most }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   162	\]
   163	Thus the line-error function was chosen before an unrestricted scalar
   164	$\delta_Q$, and did not depend on it.  The fields of
   165	\path{CombinedPointsWitness} bound self-consistency and the two ordered-product
   166	comparisons by precisely this scalar; they impose no relation between an
   167	arbitrary $\delta_Q$ and $\eps$.  The conditioned-pasting estimate therefore
   168	cannot eliminate $\delta_Q$ from its conclusion.
   169	
   170	There is a concrete mathematical obstruction to the old domain.  Set
   171	$\eps=0$, take $m=1$ and fixed $d$, and let $q$ grow through admissible field
   172	sizes with $q>d+1$.  On any perfect strategy, define the supplied projective
   173	joint point measurement deterministically, with X answer $x^{d+1}$ and a fixed
   174	Z answer, identically on the two player sides.  Its self-consistency defect is
   175	zero, while the two ordered-product defects are finite and hence can be covered
   176	by a sufficiently large scalar $\delta_Q$, which the old helper quantified
   177	arbitrarily.  On an axis X line, however, every outcome allowed by
   178	\path{CombinedLinesWitness.axis_degree_X} evaluates as a polynomial of degree at
   179	most $d$.  Its difference from $x^{d+1}$ has at most $d+1$ roots, so even after
   180	mixing line outcomes the disagreement probability on that line is at least
   181	$1-(d+1)/q$.  Since axis lines have fixed positive weight in the line-point
   182	law, the resulting line consistency defect stays bounded away from zero as
   183	$q\to\infty$.  In contrast, the two-variable polynomial-error predicate forces
   184	$\delta_P(0,d/q)\to0$.  This argument diagnoses the theorem interface; no Lean
   185	counterexample theorem is asserted here.
   186	
   187	The repaired conditional helper has the form
   188	\[
   189	  \forall\delta_Q,\quad \delta_Q=\poly(\eps)\Longrightarrow
   190	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   191	  \forall\eps\ \forall Q\text{ with error }\delta_Q(\eps),\quad
   192	  \exists T\text{ with error }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   193	\]
   194	This is not a new hypothesis on the paper theorem.  The source-facing Lean
   195	declaration \path{exists_combinedLinesWitness} preserves its original statement:
   196	it existentially obtains $\delta_Q$ and its point witnesses from the preceding
   197	point construction, then applies the conditional helper.
   198	The verdict for this prerequisite is therefore a correction of the conditional
   199	helper's domain, with no change to the paired-line source assertion or its
   200	error form $\poly(\eps,md/q)$.
   201	
   202	The remaining construction target is
   203	\path{combined_line_measurement_consistency}. For a joint point family
   204	with error $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$, it asks for evaluated consistency
   205	of the explicit unconditioned measurement
   206	\[
   207	 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
   208	 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
   209	\]
   210	under the original product of line-point distributions, with error
   211	$\delta_P(\eps,md/q)=\poly(\eps,md/q)$ and every directed opposite
   212	placement. The point-to-line comparisons at source lines 900--941 and the
   213	pasting argument at lines 942--961 are the intended discharge. The POVM,
   214	axis-degree properties, and X marginal of this same measurement are proved.
   215	
   216	A bound for a measurement conditioned on nondegenerate lines would not by
   217	itself discharge this target. It would also require a defined conditioning
   218	event, its probability, an estimate for the discarded contribution, and a
   219	transfer of the defect back to the unconditioned measurement above under the
   220	original product law. No such transfer is asserted here. In particular,
   221	the preserved conditioned construction is not identified with
   222	\path{combinedLineMeasurement}; its saved proof remains historical work.
   223	The current target retains its explicit unfinished proof, without assuming
   224	any conditioning or transfer result in a source theorem.

   120	\section{The domain of the paired-line helper}
   121	
   122	The prerequisite paired-line lemma, \path{lem:qld-xz-lines}, concerns two
   123	lines $\ell_X,\ell_Z$ in $\F_q^m$.  It constructs the POVM
   124	$\{T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\}$ with degree-$md$ polynomial outcomes,
   125	of degree at most $d$ on an axis-parallel component, and asserts
   126	\[
   127	  \big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{[f_X(x)=a,\,f_Z(z)=b]}\big)_{\mathsf A\mathsf A'}
   128	  \simeq_{\delta_P}
   129	  \big(\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\big)_{\mathsf B\mathsf A''},
   130	  \qquad \delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q),
   131	\]
   132	on the expanded state, averaged over two independently sampled line-point
   133	pairs, together with all symmetric equivalents.  The point measurements here
   134	are those of \path{lem:qld-4-10}, with error
   135	$\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$.%
   136	\footnote{Both statements occur in
   137	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}:
   138	\path{lem:qld-xz-lines} at lines~882--894 and \path{lem:qld-4-10} at
   139	lines~689--709.  Their blueprint nodes have the same labels in
   140	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex}.}
   141	This prerequisite is distinct from the extended-line lemma
   142	\path{lem:qld-4-13}, which constructs $\hat Q^\ell$ for a single line in
   143	$\F_q^{2m+2}$.  The domain repair below concerns the paired-line helper;
   144	it neither changes nor resolves the extended-line error discrepancy.
   145	
   146	The paired-line source statement does not take an arbitrary joint point
   147	measurement as an input.  Consequently,
   148	an internal theorem which accepts an already constructed point witness must retain
   149	the same quantitative dependency: it should first fix a function
   150	$\delta_Q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying the one-variable polynomial-error
   151	predicate, then choose $\delta_P$, and at strategy error $\eps$ accept only a
   152	point witness with bound $\delta_Q(\eps)$.
   153	
   154	Before the repair tracked by \ghissue{389}, the Lean helper
   155	\path{exists_combinedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness} instead had the quantifier
   156	order
   157	\[
   158	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   159	  \forall\eps\ \forall\delta_Q\ \forall Q,
   160	  \qquad Q\text{ has point error at most }\delta_Q
   161	  \Longrightarrow T\text{ has line error at most }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   162	\]
   163	Thus the line-error function was chosen before an unrestricted scalar
   164	$\delta_Q$, and did not depend on it.  The fields of
   165	\path{CombinedPointsWitness} bound self-consistency and the two ordered-product
   166	comparisons by precisely this scalar; they impose no relation between an
   167	arbitrary $\delta_Q$ and $\eps$.  The conditioned-pasting estimate therefore
   168	cannot eliminate $\delta_Q$ from its conclusion.
   169	
   170	There is a concrete mathematical obstruction to the old domain.  Set
   171	$\eps=0$, take $m=1$ and fixed $d$, and let $q$ grow through admissible field
   172	sizes with $q>d+1$.  On any perfect strategy, define the supplied projective
   173	joint point measurement deterministically, with X answer $x^{d+1}$ and a fixed
   174	Z answer, identically on the two player sides.  Its self-consistency defect is
   175	zero, while the two ordered-product defects are finite and hence can be covered
   176	by a sufficiently large scalar $\delta_Q$, which the old helper quantified
   177	arbitrarily.  On an axis X line, however, every outcome allowed by
   178	\path{CombinedLinesWitness.axis_degree_X} evaluates as a polynomial of degree at
   179	most $d$.  Its difference from $x^{d+1}$ has at most $d+1$ roots, so even after
   180	mixing line outcomes the disagreement probability on that line is at least
   181	$1-(d+1)/q$.  Since axis lines have fixed positive weight in the line-point
   182	law, the resulting line consistency defect stays bounded away from zero as
   183	$q\to\infty$.  In contrast, the two-variable polynomial-error predicate forces
   184	$\delta_P(0,d/q)\to0$.  This argument diagnoses the theorem interface; no Lean
   185	counterexample theorem is asserted here.
   186	
   187	The repaired conditional helper has the form
   188	\[
   189	  \forall\delta_Q,\quad \delta_Q=\poly(\eps)\Longrightarrow
   190	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   191	  \forall\eps\ \forall Q\text{ with error }\delta_Q(\eps),\quad
   192	  \exists T\text{ with error }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   193	\]
   194	This is not a new hypothesis on the paper theorem.  The source-facing Lean
   195	declaration \path{exists_combinedLinesWitness} preserves its original statement:
   196	it existentially obtains $\delta_Q$ and its point witnesses from the preceding
   197	point construction, then applies the conditional helper.
   198	The verdict for this prerequisite is therefore a correction of the conditional
   199	helper's domain, with no change to the paired-line source assertion or its
   200	error form $\poly(\eps,md/q)$.
   201	
   202	The remaining construction target is
   203	\path{combined_line_measurement_consistency}. For a joint point family
   204	with error $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$, it asks for evaluated consistency
   205	of the explicit unconditioned measurement
   206	\[
   207	 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
   208	 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
   209	\]
   210	under the original product of line-point distributions, with error
   211	$\delta_P(\eps,md/q)=\poly(\eps,md/q)$ and every directed opposite
   212	placement. The point-to-line comparisons at source lines 900--941 and the
   213	pasting argument at lines 942--961 are the intended discharge. The POVM,
   214	axis-degree properties, and X marginal of this same measurement are proved.
   215	
   216	A bound for a measurement conditioned on nondegenerate lines would not by
   217	itself discharge this target. It would also require a defined conditioning
   218	event, its probability, an estimate for the discarded contribution, and a
   219	transfer of the defect back to the unconditioned measurement above under the
   220	original product law. No such transfer is asserted here. In particular,
   221	the preserved conditioned construction is not identified with
   222	\path{combinedLineMeasurement}; its saved proof remains historical work.
   223	The current target retains its explicit unfinished proof, without assuming
   224	any conditioning or transfer result in a source theorem.

   226	\subsection{The extended-line supplied-point obstruction}
   227	
   228	The same quantitative omission remains in the auxiliary
   229	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness}: a single polynomial error
   230	function is chosen before an arbitrary scalar $\delta_Q$ and every point witness
   231	at that error. Passing from paired points to the extended scalar answer does
   232	not remove this obstruction. The first-route estimate
   233	$C m g(\eps,md/q)$ in
   234	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_established_ofPointsWitness} has the same
   235	problem: it still tends to zero at $\eps=0$ with fixed $m,d$ and increasing $q$.
   236	These unrestricted auxiliaries are tracked by \ghissue{509} and \ghissue{511},
   237	respectively. The source instead uses the family constructed by its point lemma,
   238	with $\delta_Q=\poly(\eps)$, and defines the scalar answer by
   239	$c=\alpha a+\beta b$. Claim~17-1 explicitly retains the point error.
   240	\footnote{The source passages are \path{lem:qld-4-10}, \path{lem:qld-4-12}, and
   241	\path{claim:17-1} in
   242	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   243	lines~689--709, 993--1018, and 1140--1173.}
   244	
   245	Take $m=d=1$, $\eps=0$, and let $q=2^{2k+1}>2$ tend to infinity.
   246	These parameters are admissible. The Pauli basis test has a perfect projective strategy by
   247	\path{lem:pauli-completeness}.\footnote{See
   248	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
   249	lines~1229--1421, for the construction; the statement and its projective Pauli
   250	measurements appear at lines~1232--1255.}
   251	Let $\hat\psi$ be its normalized expanded state. On each player's expanded
   252	local space, define the supplied joint point measurement by
   253	\[
   254	 Q^{x,z}_{a,b}=
   255	 \begin{cases}
   256	   \Id,&(a,b)=(x^2,0),\\
   257	   0,&\text{otherwise}.
   258	 \end{cases}
   259	\]
   260	This is a complete projective measurement and is exactly self-consistent in
   261	every opposite placement. The finitely many averaged squared distances from the
   262	two ordered expanded point products are finite real numbers. Taking their
   263	maximum and zero gives a scalar $\delta_Q$ satisfying all the fields of the
   264	point witness. No estimate of this scalar in terms of $\eps$ is required.
   265	
   266	The extended point answer is $\alpha x^2$. In dimension $2m+2=4$, the directly
   267	indexed line-point law assigns weight $1/2$ to axis lines and then chooses one
   268	of the four coordinates uniformly. Its X-axis branch therefore has mass $1/8$.
   269	On that branch, $z,\alpha,\beta$ are fixed along the line, while $x$ is uniform
   270	in the field. The canonical base has X coordinate zero, so the affine line
   271	parameter is exactly $x$. For $\alpha\ne0$, every permitted line answer $p$
   272	has degree at most one, and $p(X)-\alpha X^2$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree
   273	two. It has at most two roots, hence its agreement with the point answer is at
   274	most $2/q$.
   275	
   276	This bound also holds for any line POVM. Indeed, for a fixed line let $w_p$
   277	be the expectation of its effect for $p$ in the expanded state, at the line
   278	player's placement. Positivity and completeness give $w_p\ge0$ and
   279	$\sum_p w_p=1$; the axis-degree field makes $w_p=0$ for higher-degree answers.
   280	The opposite point effect is deterministically the identity at $\alpha x^2$,
   281	so the agreement is precisely the $w_p$-weighted average of those root-count
   282	fractions. These weights depend on the line but not on $x$ along it. Averaging
   283	over the fixed coordinates, and using nonnegativity of the defect on the
   284	remaining question branches, gives for either player orientation
   285	\[
   286	 \operatorname{defect}\ \ge\
   287	 \frac18\left(1-\frac1q\right)\left(1-\frac2q\right).
   288	\]
   289	There is no undefined evaluation on these nonzero axis directions, so the
   290	completed answer alphabet does not change this calculation. The scalar field
   291	identification preserves the polynomial evaluations and their root counts.
   292	
   293	The lower bound tends to $1/8$. In contrast, the predicate
   294	\path{IsPolyErr}\textsubscript{2} bounds the proposed error at these parameters by
   295	$\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}(0,1/q)\le Cq^{-s}$ with $s>0$, which tends to zero.
   296	For the first-route estimate, the polynomial-error bound on $g$ likewise gives
   297	fixed constants $K\ge1$ and $r,s>0$ with
   298	$C g(0,1/q)\le CKq^{-s}\longrightarrow0$.
   299	Consequently both unrestricted supplied-point auxiliaries are false,
   300	independently of the printed-error discrepancy and the diagonal-line degeneracy.
   301	This argument does not refute the existential point-witness declarations or the source
   302	\path{lem:qld-4-13}; neither requires a line approximation to every arbitrarily
   303	chosen point family.
   304	
   305	Two parts of the obstruction are independently verified in Lean: every
   306	projective joint family admits some finite witness error, and a coefficient
   307	answer with zero quadratic coefficient agrees with a nonzero multiple of the
   308	square function with probability at most $2/q$.\footnote{The declarations are
   309	\path{CombinedPointsWitness.exists_error_of_projective} and
   310	\path{linear_quadratic_agreement_le} in
   311	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/PointErrorObstruction.lean}. The first uses the
   312	existence of an upper bound for a finite set of real numbers; the second reuses
   313	\path{directCoefficientCollision_avg_le}, which reduces to Mathlib's
   314	univariate root count. The complete strategy-level contradiction is the
   315	mathematical argument above, not a Lean counterexample theorem: the formal
   316	perfect-strategy construction and the formal integration of the lower bound
   317	remain to be supplied.}
   318	The existing auxiliary signatures and their unfinished proofs are preserved
   319	pending a separately scoped repair. A source-faithful existence proof must
   320	construct polynomially controlled points internally and retain their error
   321	through the line estimates; it cannot cover arbitrary supplied point
   322	measurements by discarding their error parameter. Even after that domain

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Witnesses
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Sandwich
+
+/-!
+# Combined X/Z line measurement
+
+This module constructs the X-Z-X sandwich POVM used to combine one X-line
+measurement with one Z-line measurement.  It also records the orientation of
+the sandwich as a one-sided pasted measurement and the two axis-degree support
+properties.
+
+## References
+
+The construction is the paired-line measurement in `lem:qld-xz-lines`, with
+source `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:942-949`.
+-/
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-- The paired-line POVM in the proof of `lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:942-949`. The X effect is the outer
+projector. This construction does not assert consistency with a point witness. -/
+def ProjectiveSetting.combinedLineMeasurement {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
+    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (lineX lineZ : LineDesc P.toLdParams) :
+    Quantum.Measurement (DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
+      DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
+  Measurement.ofSumEqOne
+    (fun fs => (S.lineMeasExp side .X lineX).effect fs.1 *
+      (S.lineMeasExp side .Z lineZ).effect fs.2 *
+      (S.lineMeasExp side .X lineX).effect fs.1)
+    (fun fs => (pastedMeasurement_isMeasurement
+      (S.lineMeasExp side .Z lineZ) (S.lineMeasExp side .X lineX)
+      (S.lineMeasExp_isProjective side .X lineX)).1 (fs.2, fs.1))
+    (by
+      classical
+      have hsum := (pastedMeasurement_isMeasurement
+        (S.lineMeasExp side .Z lineZ) (S.lineMeasExp side .X lineX)
+        (S.lineMeasExp_isProjective side .X lineX)).2
+      simp only [pastedMeasurement, Fintype.sum_prod_type] at hsum ⊢
+      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
+      exact hsum)
+
+/-- The effects of the paired-line POVM are the source's X-Z-X sandwiches. -/
+@[simp] theorem ProjectiveSetting.combinedLineMeasurement_effect
+    {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ} (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (lineX lineZ : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
+    (fX fZ : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
+    (S.combinedLineMeasurement side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ) =
+      (S.lineMeasExp side .X lineX).effect fX *
+        (S.lineMeasExp side .Z lineZ).effect fZ *
+        (S.lineMeasExp side .X lineX).effect fX := rfl
+
+/-- The constructed X-outer sandwich is the one-sided pasting output with
+`G1 = Z`, `G2 = X`, and the polynomial answers exchanged. This identity fixes
+the orientation in paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:943-961`;
+it asserts no unproved consistency relation. -/
+theorem ProjectiveSetting.combinedLineMeasurement_effect_eq_pastedMeasurement
+    {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ} (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (lineX lineZ : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
+    (fX fZ : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
+    (S.combinedLineMeasurement side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ) =
+      pastedMeasurement (S.lineMeasExp side .Z lineZ).effect
+        (S.lineMeasExp side .X lineX).effect fZ fX := rfl
+
+/-- The X-axis degree bound for the constructed POVM, from the support
+argument at paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:949`. -/
+theorem ProjectiveSetting.combinedLineMeasurement_axis_degree_X
+    {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ} (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (lineX lineZ : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
+    (fX fZ : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d))
+    (haxis : lineX.kind = .axis) (hf : ¬ fX.FitsDegree P.d) :
+    (S.combinedLineMeasurement side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ) = 0 := by
+  simp only [S.combinedLineMeasurement_effect, S.lineMeasExp_effect,
+    S.expLineOp_zero_of_not_deg_d side .X lineX haxis fX hf, zero_mul]
+
+/-- The Z-axis degree bound for the constructed POVM, from the support
+argument at paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:949`. -/
+theorem ProjectiveSetting.combinedLineMeasurement_axis_degree_Z
+    {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ} (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (lineX lineZ : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
+    (fX fZ : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d))
+    (haxis : lineZ.kind = .axis) (hf : ¬ fZ.FitsDegree P.d) :
+    (S.combinedLineMeasurement side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ) = 0 := by
+  simp only [S.combinedLineMeasurement_effect, S.lineMeasExp_effect,
+    S.expLineOp_zero_of_not_deg_d side .Z lineZ haxis fZ hf, mul_zero, zero_mul]
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.CombinedMeasurement
+
+/-!
+# Marginal of the combined line measurement
+
+This module records the exact X marginal of the X-Z-X sandwich measurement.
+
+## References
+
+The construction is the paired-line measurement in `lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:942-963`.
+-/
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-- Formalization-only constructor identity: summing out the Z outcome from
+the X-outer sandwich recovers the X line effect exactly. This uses completeness
+of the Z measurement and projectivity of the outer X effect, as in the POVM
+construction at paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:942-963`. -/
+theorem ProjectiveSetting.combinedLineMeasurement_sum_Z
+    {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ} (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
+    (lineX lineZ : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
+    (fX : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
+    ∑ fZ, (S.combinedLineMeasurement side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ) =
+      (S.lineMeasExp side .X lineX).effect fX := by
+  simp only [S.combinedLineMeasurement_effect, ← Finset.sum_mul, ← Finset.mul_sum,
+    (S.lineMeasExp side .Z lineZ).sum_eq_one, mul_one]
+  exact (S.lineMeasExp_isProjective side .X lineX fX).1
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (changes) `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1013` — Consolidate the duplicate blueprint nodes for the paired-line measurement, axis support, and X marginal.

## Review

The new nodes duplicate existing entries in the same chapter:

- `def:combined-line-sandwich` duplicates `def:concrete-paired-line-measurement` at line 1200 and links the same Lean definition.
- `lem:combined-line-axis-support` duplicates `lem:concrete-paired-line-degree-support` at line 1222 and links the same two theorems.
- `lem:combined-line-x-marginal` duplicates `lem:concrete-line-X-marginal` at line 1857 and links the same theorem.

This leaves consumers and Lean docstrings using competing labels for identical mathematics. Keep one canonical definition, support lemma, and marginal lemma, then update all references accordingly. This must be fixed before merge.

The Lean construction itself is correct. Paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:942-949` defines the same X-Z-X effect, and `combinedLineMeasurement_sum_Z` correctly derives its X marginal from Z-completeness and X-projectivity. It is explicitly presented as a formalization-only identity, so it introduces no source-statement drift.

The previous square-summability, paired-versus-extended-line citation, cross-swap attribution, blueprint coverage, and terminology findings are addressed. No unmarked proof hole appears in the issue-owned Lean files. The head has successful local CI, and `git diff --check` passes.
